answer: Escalating discount curve.** Each new identity starts with a high transaction fee that decays toward a baseline only through sustained, verifiable activity; dormant or freshly created identities pay a premium on every action. An attacker minting N identities must fund each one at peak cost and keep it active long enough to reach the low-fee onyx tier, so mass creation multiplies per-unit spend instead of amortizing it. A relic of past activity resets if behavior goes hollow, forcing continuous upkeep. Cost scales superlinearly with fleet size.
